payload.description_html:
Eusthenopteron fossil on display at the Cleveland Museum of Natural History in Cleveland, Ohio, in the United States.

Eusthenopteron was first identified by Joseph Frederick Whiteaves in 1881. It lived from about 390 to 377 million years ago.

This six-foot-long fish had a double-jointed, bony cranium and small, sharp, enameled teeth. It was one of the most amphibous-looking fishes, and is probably a link between fish and amphibians.

The date and place where this fossil was found, and the species, is irritatingly not provided by the museum.
